explanation: Its bronze gears, more than 2,000 years old, tracked the Sun, the Moon and the cycle of the Olympic Games. Sponge divers found it in 1901, and nothing as intricate survives for centuries after.

claims.text: The Antikythera mechanism was a geared device that predicted eclipses and modelled the movements of the Sun and Moon.
The Antikythera mechanism was not a navigation, speed-measuring or weighing device.
The Antikythera mechanism's bronze gears are more than 2,000 years old.
One of the mechanism's dials tracked the four-year cycle of the Olympic Games.
Sponge divers recovered the mechanism from the wreck in 1901.
No surviving device of comparable gearing is known for many centuries after the Antikythera mechanism.
